project_comments.note: WP-001 and WP-002 were found in COMPLETE status when QA began, despite having no QA pipelines — a process anomaly (QA cannot reopen COMPLETE WPs). Their implementations were verified indirectly: (a) all 28 ledger-store tests and 27 api.test.ts tests pass (covering the WP-001 archiveDocuments() unit tests and WP-002 handleGetPlanDocument() unit tests), and (b) both are exercised end-to-end by WP-003 and WP-004 integration tests. No code defects were found in either implementation. The Reviewer should be aware that formal QA pipeline records for WP-001 and WP-002 are absent from the ledger.

REQUIRES PM ACTION: WP-001 and WP-002 are COMPLETE without QA pipelines. The ledger correctly identifies them as needing QA (ledger_get_next_action returns RUN_QA for both), but ledger_start_pipeline rejects with 'Only IN_PROGRESS work packages can have pipelines started.' QA cannot reopen COMPLETE WPs — only the PM can (COMPLETE→IN_PROGRESS). To unblock QA formality: PM should reopen both WPs, then QA agent can run formal pipelines. Alternatively, PM may accept the indirect verification (all 529 tests pass, code inspected) and mark both COMPLETE as-is. Implementations are functionally sound.

Cross-cutting pattern across WP-001 (archiveDocuments) and WP-002 (handleGetPlanDocument): both rely on a hardcoded 'plan.md' string as the archive filename. If the archive format ever adds additional documents or renames plan.md, both sides must be updated in sync. Consider extracting a shared PLAN_ARCHIVE_FILENAME constant (or a more general ARCHIVE_FILENAMES registry) in a shared utils/constants file as the system grows. Additionally, both implementations catch all errors in catch-all blocks (no ENOENT discrimination). For production hardening, differentiating ENOENT from other I/O errors (permissions, disk-full) would improve observability and error attribution across both the storage layer and the GUI API.

Synthesis complete. All 5 WPs delivered with 529/529 tests passing and 26/26 acceptance criteria met. Key cross-cutting findings: (1) hardcoded 'plan.md'/'synthesis.md' strings appear in three independent locations — a shared constant refactor is recommended; (2) archiveDocuments() catch-all error handling conflates ENOENT with other I/O failures — error message misleads; (3) handleGetPlanDocument() slug parameter used in path.join() without sanitization — medium-priority security hygiene; (4) route insertion order in server.ts is undocumented — future regression risk. Full report saved to synthesis.md.
